planes.name: Delivery
planes.question: Which operational bodies and service or data rails carry an authorised function?
planes.description: Maps departments, public bodies, shared digital products, APIs, open data and official statistics without treating technology as legal authority.

planes.name: Jurisdiction
planes.question: Which legislature, executive or local system may act for this territory and exact matter?
planes.description: Keeps the asymmetric devolution settlements and four local-government systems separate; topic resemblance is not a competence test.

planes.name: Law
planes.question: What kind of instrument carries the rule and what route made it?
planes.description: Separates Acts, statutory instruments, codes, manuals, standards and adjudication, with legislation-status warnings.

planes.name: Mandate
planes.question: How are democratic representation, Commons confidence and executive accountability connected?
planes.description: Maps institutions and constitutional relations without people, parties, current officeholders or inferred personal power.

planes.name: Money
planes.question: Which authority, forecast, control, fund, settlement and audit rail is being described?
planes.description: Keeps taxing and spending authority, fiscal analysis, central funds, banking, payment settlement, accounts, audit and scrutiny distinct.

planes.name: Remedy
planes.question: Is the route a complaint, review, appeal, ombudsman process, information right or judicial review?
planes.description: Maps typed official start doors and warns that routes are not one ladder and that deadlines and eligibility vary.

flows.name: Representation, confidence and government
flows.entry: A UK general election is held under the applicable election law.
flows.exit: A government remains accountable to Parliament and dependent on Commons confidence.

steps.name: Election returns the House of Commons
steps.caveat: This atlas has no party, candidate or result data.

steps.name: Crown performs the constitutional appointment role
steps.caveat: Conventions cannot be reduced to a party-seat algorithm.

steps.name: Government coordinates minister-led departments and functions within remit
steps.caveat: Public bodies have body-specific independence and accountability; no universal Cabinet direction or current officeholder is encoded.

steps.name: Parliament scrutinises government
steps.caveat: Scrutiny mechanisms vary and are not exhaustively mapped.

flows.name: UK primary legislation
flows.jurisdiction: United Kingdom with bill-specific territorial extent
flows.entry: A Bill enters the applicable parliamentary route.
flows.exit: An approved Bill receives Royal Assent and becomes an Act, with commencement still to be checked.

steps.name: Bill is introduced
steps.caveat: Starting House and procedure depend on Bill type.

steps.name: Parliamentary stages and agreement
steps.caveat: Detailed procedure is outside this finite overview.

steps.name: Royal Assent
steps.caveat: Assent does not mean every provision commences immediately.

steps.name: Status and effects checked
steps.caveat: Amendments, commencement, extent and outstanding effects remain provision-specific.

flows.name: Statutory-instrument route
flows.entry: An enabling Act supplies a delegated power.
flows.exit: An instrument is made and follows the specified procedure, subject to status checks.

steps.name: Locate enabling power
steps.caveat: No power is inferred from an institutional role page.

steps.name: Draft within the power and competence
steps.caveat: Maker, consultation and territorial rules vary.

steps.name: Follow specified statutory-instrument procedure
steps.caveat: Affirmative, negative and other routes are not interchangeable.

steps.name: Check made, laid, commenced and amended state
steps.caveat: A publication page is not proof of current force.

flows.name: Devolution competence routing
flows.entry: A proposed function or provision has an exact legal text and territorial application.
flows.exit: The relevant statutory competence test and institution-specific procedure are identified, or the map records an unknown.

steps.name: Identify territory and institution
steps.caveat: A policy topic alone cannot decide this step.

steps.name: Apply the settlement's exact competence test
steps.caveat: Reservations, restrictions, protected enactments and other limits differ.

steps.name: Use the legislature or executive route within competence
steps.caveat: This atlas does not decide competence for a live proposal.

steps.name: Keep local-government route nation-specific
steps.caveat: England's council guide is not reused for devolved nations.

flows.name: Central tax policy to administration
flows.jurisdiction: UK central taxes, subject to tax-specific and devolved scope
flows.entry: A policy proposal is developed under the applicable fiscal and legal process.
flows.exit: HMRC administers an enacted and commenced rule through its statutory systems and guidance.

steps.name: Treasury leads strategic tax policy
steps.caveat: This map includes no current rate or Budget prediction.

steps.name: Independent fiscal analysis informs the fiscal event
steps.caveat: Forecasting does not authorise tax.

steps.name: Parliament provides legal authority
steps.caveat: Tax-specific procedure and territorial scope must be checked.

steps.name: HMRC implements and administers
steps.caveat: No liability calculation, filing or account access occurs here.

steps.name: Review and appeal doors remain distinct
steps.caveat: Deadlines and eligibility vary by decision.

flows.name: Plan to Parliamentary Supply
flows.entry: Government develops fiscal and departmental spending plans.
flows.exit: Parliament authorises bounded resources and cash through Supply and appropriation.

steps.name: Fiscal and spending plan
steps.caveat: A plan is not authority or outturn.

steps.name: Independent forecast and analysis
steps.caveat: Forecasts do not grant Supply.

steps.name: Departments present Estimates
steps.caveat: Amounts have specific boundaries and periods.

steps.name: Commons and Parliament approve Supply
steps.caveat: This is not a retail payment instruction.

steps.name: Appropriation bounds use
steps.caveat: Virements, contingencies and supplementary routes are not exhaustively mapped.

flows.name: Authorised central-fund issue
flows.entry: Parliamentary and statutory authority exists for an issue.
flows.exit: Cash is issued under the public-finance control chain for use by the authorised body.

steps.name: Authority and appropriation exist
steps.caveat: No authority is inferred from a payment request.

steps.name: Central fund records the public cash position
steps.caveat: The fund is not a labelled-pound tracing ledger.

steps.name: Comptroller function grants credit for an authorised issue
steps.caveat: Exact statutory provision and fund must be checked.

steps.name: Treasury issues within authority
steps.caveat: Issue is distinct from departmental outturn and service delivery.

steps.name: Department accounts for use
steps.caveat: Accounts and audit follow separate records and periods.

flows.name: Operational banking and payment rails
flows.entry: A public body already has legal authority and an operational payment need.
flows.exit: A banking or payment system carries the transaction under its own participation and control framework.

steps.name: Separate authority from payment instruction
steps.caveat: The atlas creates neither.

steps.name: Government Banking Service supports public bodies
steps.caveat: No account or provider credential is exposed.

steps.name: Payment systems exchange and settle obligations
steps.caveat: RTGS and CHAPS access is not provided.

steps.name: Regulation remains distinct from operation
steps.caveat: No regulatory determination is made.

flows.name: Authorised function to digital service
flows.entry: A public body has an identified function, legal basis, controller and service owner.
flows.exit: A service uses selected operational rails while authority and accountability stay with the responsible body.

steps.name: Identify body, function and legal basis
steps.caveat: A directory or API listing does not prove authority.

steps.name: Design against service and technology standards
steps.caveat: Standards are not silently promoted to legislation.

steps.name: Select identity, forms, messaging or payment capabilities
steps.caveat: This atlas embeds none of those functions.

steps.name: Publish API or data discovery metadata where appropriate
steps.caveat: Rights, quality and availability remain dataset-specific.

steps.name: Retain accountable decision and remedy routes
steps.caveat: Technology does not become the legal decision-maker by carrying data.

flows.name: Typed redress route selection
flows.entry: A person identifies the exact decision, service failure, information request or alleged public-law error.
flows.exit: The person reaches the official start page for a potentially relevant route and checks current eligibility and deadline.

steps.name: Classify issue without merging routes
steps.caveat: The atlas does not determine eligibility.

steps.name: Protect any statutory review or appeal deadline
steps.caveat: A complaint may not stop an appeal clock.

steps.name: Use complaint or ombudsman route only within remit
steps.caveat: Prior complaint steps and territorial jurisdiction vary.

steps.name: Use information-rights route for recorded information
steps.caveat: Exemptions and internal-review requirements vary.

steps.name: Seek legal advice for judicial review
steps.caveat: The mapped CPR route is England and Wales only and strict time limits apply.

rails.name: Election and Commons-confidence rail
rails.description: Connects representation, constitutional appointment, ministerial direction and parliamentary accountability without party or person data.

rails.name: Asymmetric devolution rail
rails.description: Routes an exact provision through the relevant statutory competence framework rather than topic matching.

rails.name: Primary and delegated law rail
rails.description: Separates Bill, Act, enabling power, statutory instrument, commencement and status.

rails.name: Data discovery and official-statistics rail
rails.description: Keeps API discovery, dataset publication, statistics governance, source rights and personal-data law distinct.

rails.name: Supply, central-fund credit and issue rail
rails.description: Connects Parliamentary authority, the Consolidated Fund, C&AG credit, Treasury issue and departmental accounting.

rails.name: Forecast and fiscal-policy rail
rails.description: Separates independent analysis, Treasury policy, parliamentary authority and HMRC administration.

rails.name: Banking and payment-settlement rail
rails.description: Separates GBS banking, RTGS settlement, CHAPS operation and payment-system regulation from Supply and liability.

rails.name: Accounts, audit and parliamentary scrutiny rail
rails.description: Separates departmental accounts, NAO audit and Public Accounts Committee scrutiny.

rails.name: Information-rights rail
rails.description: Routes a recorded-information request through the covered authority, internal steps and eligible ICO complaint.

rails.name: Decision and public-service redress rail
rails.description: Keeps complaints, statutory reviews, appeals, ombudsmen and judicial review as typed alternatives.

rails.name: Shared digital-service rail
rails.description: Maps Service Standard, One Login, Notify, Pay, Forms and API discovery as optional operational capabilities.

redressRoutes.name: FOI request, internal steps and ICO complaint
redressRoutes.jurisdiction: Covered UK public authorities subject to the applicable information regime
prerequisites: identify the applicable information regime
follow the public authority's request and internal-review route where required

redressRoutes.name: HMRC service complaint
redressRoutes.jurisdiction: HMRC service within the published complaint remit
prerequisites: separate service dissatisfaction from a challenge to a tax decision
check whether another deadline must be protected

redressRoutes.name: HMRC statutory review where offered or available
prerequisites: identify the exact decision and notice
check whether review is offered or available and protect the stated deadline

redressRoutes.name: Judicial review in England and Wales
prerequisites: obtain current legal advice
check standing, alternative remedies, permission and urgency

redressRoutes.name: Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman
redressRoutes.jurisdiction: Councils and certain services in England within remit
prerequisites: check body, provider and subject jurisdiction
complete prior complaint steps where required

redressRoutes.name: Northern Ireland Public Services Ombudsman
redressRoutes.jurisdiction: Northern Ireland bodies and matters within remit
prerequisites: check body and subject jurisdiction
complete prior complaint steps where required

redressRoutes.name: Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman
redressRoutes.jurisdiction: UK government departments and NHS in England within remit
prerequisites: complete the organisation's complaint process where required
check jurisdiction and the Parliamentary route

redressRoutes.name: Scottish Public Services Ombudsman
prerequisites: check body and subject jurisdiction
complete prior complaint steps where required

redressRoutes.name: First-tier Tribunal tax appeal
redressRoutes.jurisdiction: Eligible UK tax decisions within tribunal jurisdiction
prerequisites: identify the appealable decision and applicable procedure
protect the decision-specific deadline

redressRoutes.name: Public Services Ombudsman for Wales
prerequisites: check body and subject jurisdiction
complete prior complaint steps where required

unknowns.question: Has a cited department, public body or service owner changed since the review date?
unknowns.reason: Live organisation directories and service ownership can change without changing the constitutional model.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: any owner, URL or machinery-of-government change

unknowns.question: Which legislature or executive has competence for a specific proposed provision?
unknowns.reason: Competence depends on exact text, purpose, effect, reservations and settlement-specific restrictions.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: an exact proposal and current statutory analysis become available

unknowns.question: Which public services currently use each shared digital product and under what data-controller arrangements?
unknowns.reason: Product pages establish capability but not a complete participation, legal-basis or controller map.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: a bounded official service contract and privacy/legal-basis record is admitted

unknowns.question: Is each cited provision commenced, amended, extended and fully updated for a live matter?
unknowns.reason: Contents pages and a dated atlas cannot guarantee current provision status or resolve outstanding effects.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: before relying on a provision for an actual matter

unknowns.question: Which exact council tier or body holds a particular function in each nation and locality?
unknowns.reason: Structures, reorganisations and statutory functions vary; Phase 0 exposes entry points, not a complete council-power graph.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: a specific locality and function are selected for source-linked expansion

unknowns.question: Can a particular receipt be traced to a particular service expenditure?
unknowns.reason: Authority, accounts, funds and payments do not generally establish a labelled-pound path from one taxpayer to one service.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: a statute or audited accounting record expressly establishes the link

unknowns.question: What route, eligibility rule and deadline applies to an actual decision or complaint?
unknowns.reason: Complaint, review, appeal, ombudsman, information-rights and judicial-review rules differ and can change.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: the exact notice, jurisdiction and current official procedure are available

unknowns.question: Has an official statistic or dataset been revised, reclassified or superseded?
unknowns.reason: Dataset discovery and institutional status do not freeze methods, quality or revision history.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: before importing any statistic or dataset into a later contract

unknowns.question: Have the selected TaxSorted records, rights, schema or release checkpoints changed since capture?
unknowns.reason: The captures are digest-bound but the upstream datasets do not declare immutable snapshots and were already reviewed before acquisition.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: TaxSorted publishes a new version, digest, rights statement, record ID or correction

unknowns.question: What permission and onward-appeal route applies after a First-tier Tribunal tax decision?
unknowns.reason: Phase 0 maps only the First-tier start door; Upper Tribunal and appellate-court permission routes are decision- and jurisdiction-specific.
unknowns.reviewTrigger: a bounded official Upper Tribunal and onward-appeal source contract is added
